decision: Keep Pele bundled inline; do not split a lazy runtime in 0.2.0.
rule: Adopt only if cold-start improvement is material (roadmap example: >=200 ms or >=200 KB encodedBodySize) AND first-diagram latency regression is acceptable (roadmap example: <=150 ms locally). One metric consistently on both sides. Default is no.

measurements.route: local plain-HTTP server, no content-encoding, cache-control: no-cache, one HTML + bundle.js request
measurements.routeCaveat: Local plain-HTTP fixture route, NOT the installed DSH /plugins route: no Content-Encoding and no cache headers beyond no-cache. DSH's real encoding/caching was not measurable without an authenticated installed-host route run.

cold.observed: bundle request+eval completes by ~34 ms after navigation; first diagram ready at ~395 ms (dominated by 150 ms scan debounce + 180 ms settle window, plus mount)

referenceSplitFromRoadmap.note: Historical reference numbers from a comparable implementation, not measurements of this plugin.

rationale: Measured local bundle cost (request + parse/eval) is ~12-34 ms; first-diagram latency is ~370-395 ms and is dominated by the fixed 150 ms scan debounce + 180 ms settle window, not by bundle size. Splitting Pele therefore cannot produce a >=200 ms cold-start *time* improvement on this evidence.

The byte side looks material in principle (gzip -9 276,084 B / brotli 223,848 B for the final 739,526 B inline bundle), but the installed DSH route's real Content-Encoding, cache behavior and encodedBodySize are unmeasured; the roadmap decision rule requires route-level metrics before a byte-based claim.

A split adds a host half (same-origin route, webServer injection, cache-busting ?v=<hash>, immutable caching, failure fallback) plus a client loader path and tests. That is a new architecture surface, and the roadmap's default for 0.2.0 is no unless measurements support the change; no split prototype was built to measure the first-diagram regression the rule requires.
The whole inline bundle budget (750,000 B raw) is met at 739,526 B, so keeping the inline build does not breach the 0.2.0 budget.
revisitWhen: Run PerformanceResourceTiming (encodedBodySize/transferSize/decodedBodySize), Cache-Status and Content-Encoding against the installed DSH plugin route, build a split prototype, and re-evaluate with cold-start time and first-diagram regression numbers on the same metric.
